title: Smart Squelch and Proactive Failover Orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our on-call signal surface remains noisy during transient degradations and partial-region capacity pressure. This causes unnecessary paging and manual remediation for issues that are either self-healing (cache rebuilds, transient infra blips) or low-customer-impact. Simultaneously, we lack an automated, safe coupling between alerting and our circuit-breaker/load-shedding decisions, meaning SREs must manually flip traffic or invoke fallthroughs.

Goal: Build a 'Smart Squelch' pipeline that scores, groups, and suppresses low-value alerts automatically while elevating high-impact signals. Couple that pipeline to a 'Proactive Failover Orchestration' layer that can safely trigger pre-approved circuit-breaker policies and regional load-shedding when measured SLO degradation crosses thresholds. The system should support automated playbook execution (autoresponder) for common partial failures, and seamless handoff to on-call with context when human intervention is required.
acceptance_criteria: Score-based suppression reduces P1 pages by >=60% in the synthetic noise window tests
Automated failover can be executed via playbook with an automated dry-run and a single-confirmation step
Circuit-breaker triggers and load-shedding policies are parametrized by SLO-weighted customer-impact and can be rolled back automatically if error budget consumption decreases
All actions are logged to audit trail and surfaced in console timeline and incident postmortems
On-call runbooks are converted to machine-executable playbooks for the top 8 recurring alert clusters
success_metrics: P1 paging volume (weekly) down by 50% post-rollout
Mean time to acknowledgement (MTTA) for true-production-impact incidents <= 3 minutes
False-positive page rate <= 10% of pre-rollout baseline
Automated mitigation executed without human confirmation for at least 30% of qualifying degradations in perf tests
Number of manual region failovers reduced by 70% in sim exercises
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for scoring engine and suppression rules. 2) Integration tests that inject synthetic signals across regions and assert suppression/aggregation behavior. 3) Chaos experiments to validate circuit-breaker coupling and safe rollback. 4) Canary rollout to internal prod namespace with verbose logging and manual watch for 72h. 5) Load tests verifying that load-shedding reduces tail latency and prevents downstream retries from cascading.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Deploy scoring service to staging and enable 'observe-only' suppression for 2 weeks. Phase 2: Enable soft-squelch where suppressed alerts are grouped and routed to a quiet Slack channel with digesting rules. Phase 3: Enable auto-remediation for low-risk clusters with 1-click escalation. Phase 4: Gradually enable automated failover coupling in a single region with a dry-run-only mode, then enable single-confirmation mode, then full automatic mode for pre-approved policies. Phase 5: Full rollout to multi-region with SLO gating and canary fade-in over 7 days.
notes: Key design trade-offs: 1) Balance between reducing noise and hiding novel regressions — we will keep anomaly-score thresholds conservative for first two cycles and surface suppressed signals in a digest so humans can audit. 2) Automated failover must be reversible — every action has a built-in rollback plan and time-limited scope. 3) Auditability: all automated decisions are tied to change-IDs and logged to both central observability and the console timeline. 4) Dependency on circuit-breaker primitives: ENG-654321 implements route-level breakers; we will call that API rather than embedding new breakers.
